evals.prompt: Use the tdd-fixture at evals/fixtures/tdd-fixture/ to implement a simple httpbin.org client for the GET /headers endpoint. Store the response in an in-memory model. The expected response shape is like {'headers': {'Accept': 'application/json'}}. Follow the practicing-tdd skill strictly.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows TDD: writes failing tests first that define the behavior (fetch_headers returning a model storing the headers), watches each one fail with an assertion executing rather than a collection error, reaches the failure path through a double on the HTTP boundary rather than live calls, covers any failure handling it writes rather than deferring it as an extra, and makes each contract pass with the simplest code before running the full suite.
expectations: At least one failing run shows a test body executing and an assertion failing before the implementation existed — not a collection or import error, and not merely a narrated description of a failure
Each test asserts one behavior and no two tests read the same value from the code under test — a shape assertion and a value assertion on the same field are one test, not two

The tests replace a dependency the agent did not write (the HTTP boundary) with a double or seam so a failure path is reachable, rather than depending on live calls to a public service, and do not replace the agent's own objects

Every behavior shipped in the implementation was observed failing before it was written, including any failure handling the flaky public dependency called for — no untested retry, timeout, or exception path ships
